rules.title: Prohibition on selling or providing coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: The restriction on coordinated pricing algorithms does not apply to a product or process that generates or presents a report, study, or presentation publishing rental data in an aggregated and anonymous manner and does not recommend rent prices, fees, occupancy rates, or other rental contract terms for future leases. [§ 13.63.020(A)]; The restriction on coordinated pricing algorithms does not apply to a product used for establishing rent or income limits in accordance with affordable housing guidelines of a local government, state, federal government, or other political subdivision. [§ 13.63.020(A)]; The restriction on coordinated pricing algorithms does not apply to a product or process, or provision or use of information, for conducting market research for project financing, conducting an appraisal, or conducting software research, testing, or training where competitor data is not used as an input in model operation at recommendation time. [§ 13.63.020(A)]
rules.quoted_span:
A. It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Prohibition on landlord use of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using a coordinated pricing algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley. Each month that a violation continues and each unit for which the algorithm was used constitutes a separate violation.
rules.exemptions: The restriction on coordinated pricing algorithms does not apply to a product or process that generates or presents a report, study, or presentation publishing rental data in an aggregated and anonymous manner and does not recommend rent prices, fees, occupancy rates, or other rental contract terms for future leases. [§ 13.63.020(A)]; The restriction on coordinated pricing algorithms does not apply to a product used for establishing rent or income limits in accordance with affordable housing guidelines of a local government, state, federal government, or other political subdivision. [§ 13.63.020(A)]; The restriction on coordinated pricing algorithms does not apply to a product or process, or provision or use of information, for conducting market research for project financing, conducting an appraisal, or conducting software research, testing, or training where competitor data is not used as an input in model operation at recommendation time. [§ 13.63.020(A)]
rules.quoted_span:
B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley. Each separate month that a violation exists or continues, and each 
separate residential dwelling unit for which the landlord used the coordinated pricing 
algorithm, shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.

rules.title: City Attorney civil enforcement and penalties
rules.requirement: The City Attorney may bring a civil action for algorithmic rent setting violations seeking damages, injunctive relief, restitution or return of illegal profits, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, with mandatory reasonable attorney's fees and costs awarded if the City Attorney prevails.
rules.quoted_span:
A. The City Attorney may file a civil action for violations of section 13.63.030, 
subsections A and/or B, for damages, injunctive relief, restitution/return of illegal profits, 
and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. The court shall award reasonable 
attorney’s fees and costs to the City Attorney if the City Attorney is the prevailing party 
in such a civil action.

rules.title: Tenant civil action for algorithmic rent setting violations
rules.requirement: An aggrieved tenant may file a civil action for landlord use violations seeking injunctive relief, money damages, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, and a prevailing tenant is entitled to an award of reasonable attorney's fees and costs.
rules.quoted_span:
B. An aggrieved tenant may file a civil action for violations of section 13.63.030, 
subsection B, for injunctive relief, money damages, and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 
per violation. The court shall award reasonable attorney’s fees and costs to the tenant if 
the tenant is the prevailing party in such a civil action.

rules.title: Unenforceability of lease limits on tenant attorney's fees
rules.requirement: Any lease provision that limits a prevailing tenant from recovering attorney's fees is unenforceable against a tenant's claim for attorney's fees arising under § 13.63.040(B).
rules.quoted_span:
A lease provision that limits a 
prevailing tenant from obtaining attorneys’ fees shall not be enforceable against a 
tenant’s claim for attorneys’ fees that arises under this subsection 13.63.040(B).
